subject: Standardizing local-market modifiers for offer consistency
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Anita Rao <anita.rao@benchmarkdata.co>
Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Standardizing local-market modifiers for offer consistency

Team,

We're getting more questions from hiring managers about when to apply a local-market modifier vs. a remote premium. The intent of this thread is to land on a simple decision rule we can operationalize in the offers playbook and the compensation matrix.

Key constraints:
- Keep offer velocity high (no >48h manual approvals for standard cases).
- Preserve our global budget guardrails (geo multipliers should not increase base by more than +20% for equivalent level).
- Make candidate-facing rationale clear and defensible for recruiters.

Proposal (attached comp_matrix_v4.xlsx):
1) Default: use base band for role + level tied to candidate primary work location.
2) If candidate is remote but located in a high-cost market, apply the local-market modifier for that market (instead of a generic remote premium).
3) Maintain a separate, capped remote-premium bucket (5–10%) for verified circumstance-based exceptions (e.g., retention-critical ICs, expiring counteroffers).

Asks:
- Karthik: validate ops implications for approvals and headcount cost projections.
- Lauren: sanity-check the band translations and recruiter playbook language.
- Anita (benchmark data): confirm the market multipliers and source windows.

Attached: comp_matrix_v4.xlsx (working band table) and benchmark_summary_q2.pdf

Thanks,
Marissa
Marissa Cole
Head of Talent Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Jun 2026 10:23:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Standardizing local-market modifiers for offer consistency

Marissa — thanks for the clear framing. Quick operational notes after a skim of comp_matrix_v4: 

- Approvals: If we turn on market modifiers by candidate location, we should add an automatic routing rule in Greenhouse for cases where adjusted OTE > 12% above role baseline. That preserves speed for normal hires and routes outliers for finance/compreview.
- Budget model: I ran a quick projection for Q3 hires at current req load — using your default approach bumps monthly committed spend by ~6% vs today (assuming 40% hires in higher-cost metros). We can absorb this inside the headcount plan if we: a) tighten bonus pool by 1ppt, or b) ask hiring managers to prioritize 60/40 remote-high vs. remote-low distribution.
- Edge cases: For contractor conversions, keep contractor rate conversion rules unchanged for now (we'll re-evaluate in Q4).

I'll update the playbook language for approvals and push a small automation ticket for Greenhouse routing (Jira HR-5467).

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Director, People Ops
Redwood Inference

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Anita Rao <anita.rao@benchmarkdata.co>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2026 08:44:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Standardizing local-market modifiers for offer consistency

Thanks — attaching a short recruiter-facing blurb I drafted below (we'll drop into the offers playbook):

Recruiter playbook blurb (draft):
- Use candidate primary address as the source of truth for market multiplier.
- If the candidate is remote but located in a listed high-cost market, apply that market's multiplier. Do NOT stack an additional "remote premium."
- For retention/competitive exceptions, submit a Request for Offer Override via the comp review form; approvals required: Hiring Manager -> People Ops Lead -> Finance (auto-route if +12% above baseline).

Benchmarks: Anita confirmed Q2 sources cover last 12 months and show the following sample multipliers: SF Bay Area +18%, NYC +15%, Boston +12%, Seattle +11%. She flagged that our current matrix underweights mid-level SWE comparators (we should consider a +1% uplift for L3-L4 if we want to be above market median).

I'm comfortable with the three-rule approach Marissa proposed. My only ask: explicit language for recruiter scripts so candidates don't hear "we apply a remote premium" — instead, we say "we match the market where you reside."

Attachment: recruiter_blurb_v1.txt (inline below)

Best,
Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Compensation Partner
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2026 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Standardizing local-market modifiers for offer consistency

Thanks everyone — good alignment. Final decisions we can ship to recruiters tomorrow: 

1) Go-live rules: default band by primary work location; high-cost market multiplier applies in lieu of a separate remote premium.
2) Exception channel: cap remote/exception premium at 10% (documented) and require the comp-review workflow for any >10% uplift. Auto-route anything +12% as Karthik suggested.
3) Band tweak: add +1% uplift band for L3-L4 engineers pending Anita's final CSV (she'll send by EOD).

I'll publish an updated offers playbook page and brief hiring managers + recruiters in today's standups. Grace — please coordinate comms and drop the updated recruiter script into the hiring drive link (https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1a2bCompMatrix).

Attachments referenced above: comp_matrix_v4.xlsx, benchmark_summary_q2.pdf

Marissa
Head of Talent Operations
Redwood Inference
